items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And I forget what drummer it was I reliefed there. He was an old time drummer. Oh yeah. It was Ernest Rogers, that's right.

ctx.x: They always do it the same way. They used to.

That's right. Right. That's right. You hit the first note on the right foot? Yeah, right on the right foot, yeah. What places did you play in the district? Oh, in the district? Let me see. I worked at, I didn't work regular. I mean I, I relief old man Contrell at Rice. I used to relief him there. And then I relief Henry Zeno at Pete Lala. I used to relief him there. When King Oliver had the band, Joe Oliver had the band. He wasn't King then. It was Joe, Joe Oliver. And then I played at Few Clothes a few times.…

You know, I've been about 25. Huh? No, he wasn't that old. You weren't 25 years old. No. I didn't know much. I was a little. I had to put on long pants to go play. I had to put on long pants to go play. 16 or 15 years old when he started. I don't know if he was that. No. I had to put on long pants to go play. I had to put on long pants to go play. 16 or 15 years old when he started. I don't know if he was that. No. He was stabbed in heaven. He had to put on long pants. He had to put on long pants because he was…

And then when I used to go work in the red light district. I used to go over there, he'd come and get me a little little fellow, a little kind of trouble, a friend of my union. Come at the house and tell me his dad said to go to his place at Rice's. And I put on, I had a pair of old long pants and stripes and it was heavy, big summertime, heavy piece of goods. And I put those long trousers on and go up there and play. Play with Manion and them. Manion and Francis had to wake Rice. They'd wake there a long time,…
I loved it a kid. Whose band was at Fue Clothes?
